S1.label: Structured data reasoning
S1.pattern: Fails when multiple tool results must be cross-referenced to find cheapest/shortest/most expensive option, or to match product variant specs. Most visible in flight search (finding cheapest route across airports) and product variant matching (finding correct item by attributes).

S2.label: Tool calling precision
S2.pattern: Most common failure mode. Agent selects correct tool but passes wrong item_id, flight_number, payment_id, new_item_id, or order_id. Especially frequent in exchange/modify actions where product variant IDs must be precisely matched. Right intent, wrong specific argument.

S3.label: Multi-step task completion
S3.pattern: Agent drops subtasks when handling 3+ simultaneous requests, gets distracted mid-conversation, or fails to complete all items across multiple orders. Second or third subtask often abandoned. Worse when subtasks span different orders or require sequential API calls.

S4.label: Precondition verification
S4.pattern: Dominant airline failure. Agent acts without verifying: (1) basic economy non-modifiable policy, (2) insurance reason validity, (3) refund eligibility, (4) payment method must match original. Especially susceptible to user pressure — emotional appeals or repeated insistence override policy checks.

S5.label: Numerical reasoning
S5.pattern: Arithmetic errors in computing refund amounts, compensation amounts, price differences across multiple items/reservations, and payment splitting. Particularly problematic for bulk operations (5 reservations) and payment optimization tasks.

S6.label: Record discovery and retrieval
S6.pattern: Dominant retail failure. Agent retrieves wrong order (wrong order_id when user has multiple orders), wrong product, or fails user lookup entirely. Common causes: (1) user provides name+zip but agent tries wrong zip variants, (2) agent looks up orders in wrong sequence and picks wrong matching order, (3) malformed order IDs (missing '#W' prefix).

S7.label: Information communication
S7.pattern: Agent performs correct actions and DB state is right, but fails to state specific values: refund amount, price difference, tracking number, material type, total cost. Communicate check fails even when DB passes. Often the task requires both taking action AND reporting a specific number.

S8.label: Conditional and state-aware reasoning
S8.pattern: Agent uses wrong API for the current state of the record (e.g., modify_pending on delivered order, create_order for replacement, update_reservation when cancel is required). Also fails to follow if-then policy chains (e.g., if basic economy then cancel not modify; if no refund policy then transfer not cancel).
